title: Empowering Cryo-EM Research Across the Southeastern U.S. Through SECM4
content: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has revolutionized structural biology, yet access to this technology remains limited in many regions. The Southeastern Cryo-Electron Microscopy Center (SECM4) at Florida State University addresses this challenge by providing comprehensive cryo-EM capabilities to researchers across the Southeastern United States. Our facility integrates advanced sample preparation equipment, state-of-the-art cryo-microscopes, and high-performance computing infrastructure with expert support throughout the experimental pipeline. SECM4's user training program emphasizes hands-on experience in grid preparation, microscope operation, and data processing, enabling researchers to develop independent expertise rather than relying on service-based access. The center maintains quality through external peer review of proposals while maximizing accessibility for institutions lacking local cryo-EM infrastructure. Our integrated approach has supported diverse structural biology projects, from membrane protein complexes to large macromolecular assemblies, achieving resolutions suitable for atomic model building. The facility's computational resources and on-site expertise facilitate both single-particle analysis and cryo-electron tomography workflows. Through this comprehensive support system, SECM4 not only accelerates structural biology research across the Southeast but also builds a sustainable community of skilled cryo-EM practitioners. As we expand into emerging areas such as integrative structural modeling and advanced computational methods, SECM4 continues to evolve as a catalyst for structural biology innovation in the region.
